summary: Full backend + frontend E2E for WATTLY. 21/21 backend pytest tests pass after fixing an ObjectId-mutation bug in 4 POST endpoints (purchase, link utility, credit events, payouts). Frontend pages (Landing/Marketplace/Bill/Dashboard/MyShares/Credits) all render and integrate correctly with the API. Cookie-based auth verified end-to-end.

critical_code_review_comments: FIXED IN-PLACE: motor's insert_one mutates the source dict by adding an ObjectId _id. server.py was returning these mutated dicts in 4 endpoints (POST /shares/purchase, internal credit_event insert, POST /utility/link, POST /payout/request), causing FastAPI jsonable_encoder to raise 500. Wrapped each insert_one argument with dict(...) to insert a copy and keep the original doc clean.

Datetime fields are stored as ISO strings but the Pydantic models declare datetime — works due to ConfigDict(extra='ignore') and Pydantic auto-coercion, but consistency is fragile. Consider standardizing on either bson Date or ISO strings everywhere.
seed() guard only checks farms collection emptiness — fine but won't repair partially-seeded telemetry if a previous run aborted mid-seed.
CORS allow_origins falls back to '*' when CORS_ORIGINS env missing, while allow_credentials=True — strictly speaking browsers reject this combo. In production set CORS_ORIGINS explicitly.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend ObjectId bug already patched - if you see 500s on POST /shares/purchase, /utility/link, or /payout/request again, re-check that the insert_one calls still wrap their argument in dict(). To test auth-gated endpoints, follow /app/auth_testing.md: create user+session via mongosh, then either send Authorization: Bearer <token> for curl OR set session_token cookie for browser. The pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_wattly_backend.py is the canonical regression suite (run: pytest backend/tests/test_wattly_backend.py -v).
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE (500 on insert+return endpoints): Motor's AsyncIOMotorCollection.insert_one mutates the input dict in-place to add the generated _id (bson.ObjectId). The original code (e.g., link_utility) returned that same dict, so FastAPI's jsonable_encoder hit an ObjectId and raised TypeError('ObjectId is not iterable'), surfacing as HTTP 500. REPRODUCTION: POST /api/utility/link or /api/shares/purchase with a valid session_token cookie -> 500. MITIGATION APPLIED: Wrap each insert_one() argument with dict(...) so motor mutates a throwaway copy and the original (clean) dict is returned to the client. Verified by re-running the pytest suite — all 21 tests pass; manually re-checked /api/shares/purchase + /api/utility/link return 200 with clean JSON (no _id field).
